notes: Executor harness + grading: see README.md 'Skill evals'. Each eval copies fixtures/demo-repo to a temp dir, git-inits and commits it as the seed, then a fresh subagent executes skills/run/SKILL.md as /flywheel:run in that dir. Grade with: bash skills/run/evals/check.sh <id> <workdir>. Regrading a workdir after the run's own date requires FW_EVAL_DATE=<run date> (eval 1 asserts the audited field against the run date, not the grading date).

evals.name: happy-path-persist
evals.setup: cp -r skills/run/evals/fixtures/demo-repo "$W" && git -C "$W" init -q && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e add -A && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm seed
evals.expected_output: The run follows the contract's fixed rules, persists the audit row per DATA.md and proves it, and regenerates the telemetry report.
expectations: data/plate-audits.md gains the row '| 9876 KZX | 9876 | KZX | 30 |' dated with the run date — the exact deterministic fields Rule 3 fixes
The write landed per DATA.md: data/plate-audits.md has no unstaged modification (staged or committed)
A telemetry report exists at .claude/flywheel/runs/plate-audit/<date>.html (two-tier since v0.30.0: JSONL per transition, HTML rendered at close)
The seeded row for 1234 BCD is untouched

evals.name: idempotent-upsert
evals.setup: cp -r skills/run/evals/fixtures/demo-repo "$W" && git -C "$W" init -q && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e add -A && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm seed
evals.expected_output: The plate already has a seeded row; the run updates it in place instead of appending a duplicate.
expectations: Exactly one row for plate 1234 BCD exists in data/plate-audits.md after the run
The row's deterministic fields are still digits=1234, letters=BCD, digit_sum=10
No unstaged modification of data/plate-audits.md remains

evals.name: guardrail-invalid-input
evals.setup: cp -r skills/run/evals/fixtures/demo-repo "$W" && git -C "$W" init -q && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e add -A && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm seed
evals.expected_output: AEI contains vowels, so Rule 2 fails: the run records a rejection and produces no audit row — it must not fabricate fields to look complete.
expectations: No audit row containing 'AEI' appears in the Audits table
A rejection line mentioning the input is appended under ## Rejections
The seeded row for 1234 BCD is untouched

evals.expected_output: The run refuses to start: its declared write path is probed read-only at step 1, the probe fails (the Postgres in DATA.md is not listening), and the run reports a blocker without executing any Rule — no row persisted, no partial write, no fabricated output.
evals.setup: cp -r skills/run/evals/fixtures/unreachable-store-repo "$W" && git -C "$W" init -q && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e add -A && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm seed
expectations: No audit row for 9876 KZX exists anywhere in the workdir — nothing was persisted
The seeded 1234 BCD row is byte-intact and the datastore is neither modified nor staged
No transition line records a Rule as completed: the run stopped before executing the contract, not part-way through it
No result file was created outside the declared store (no silent fallback to a second store)

evals.expected_output: The contract contradicts itself — Rule 3 computes a digit sum reaching 36 while the Output schema caps digit_sum at 0-27 — so no input of this class has a conforming output. The run stops as a blocker, leaves the contract byte-identical, does not file the valid plate as a rejection, and stubs a spec naming both conflicting clauses.
evals.setup: cp -r skills/run/evals/fixtures/contradictory-contract-repo "$W" && git -C "$W" init -q && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e add -A && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm seed
expectations: A spec stub exists under .claude/flywheel/specs/ naming both conflicting clauses (the Rule that computes digit_sum and the Output schema bound)
The contract is byte-identical: no version bump, no schema edit, no Improvement log entry — escalating is not fixing
The ## Rejections section is untouched: a contract defect is not an invalid input, and filing it as one mislabels a valid plate
The run recorded a blocker before stopping
